avoid_supplements.name: Ephedra/Ma huang
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Sympathomimetic activity antagonizes beta-blocker effects; risk of hypertensive crisis and arrhythmias
avoid_supplements.action: Absolutely contraindicated; counsel patient to avoid all ephedra-containing products

avoid_supplements.name: Yohimbe
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Alpha-2 adrenergic antagonist; counteracts beta-blockade and increases blood pressure and heart rate
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; recommend alternative supplements

avoid_supplements.name: Licorice (high doses)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Mineralocorticoid effects cause sodium retention and potassium depletion; increases blood pressure and reduces atenolol efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Restrict to minimal amounts; monitor blood pressure and electrolytes if use unavoidable

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild sympathomimetic properties and could theoretically reduce beta-blocker efficacy
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; monitor blood pressure response

caution_supplements.name: Hawthorn
caution_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate cardiovascular effects and cause additive hypotension
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for excessive blood pressure reduction; adjust doses if needed

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May enhance beta-blocker effects and cause additive hypotension
caution_supplements.action: Use standard dietary doses only; monitor blood pressure

avoid_foods.name: High-sodium foods
avoid_foods.mechanism: Excessive sodium increases fluid retention and blood pressure, reducing atenolol effectiveness in hypertension management
avoid_foods.action: Counsel on DASH diet and sodium restriction (<2.3g/day); monitor blood pressure control

caution_foods.name: Caffeine (high intake)
caution_foods.mechanism: Sympathomimetic effects may partially antagonize beta-blocker efficacy and increase heart rate variability
caution_foods.action: Limit caffeine intake to moderate levels (<200mg/day); monitor heart rate and blood pressure

caution_foods.name: Licorice-containing candies/foods
caution_foods.mechanism: High licorice consumption can cause sodium retention and potassium loss, opposing beta-blocker antihypertensive effects
caution_foods.action: Limit consumption; counsel on hidden sources in candy and herbal teas

monitoring_notes: Atenolol has minimal hepatic metabolism and is primarily renally eliminated, reducing drug-drug interaction potential via CYP pathways. Monitor for loss of blood pressure control, excessive bradycardia, and electrolyte abnormalities, particularly when supplements or dietary changes are introduced; renal function should be assessed periodically given renal dependence of elimination.
